q: Carbon is the main constituent of fossil fuels such as coal, oil and natural gas.
e: The textbook identifies carbon as the main constituent of these fossil fuels.

q: A large amount of mechanical energy is stored in the fossil fuels.
e: A large amount of chemical energy is stored in fossil fuels.

q: Coal goes through a different formation process called coalification.
e: The text specifies that coal formation involves a process called coalification.

q: Coal is made of decomposed plant matter in conditions of high temperature and pressure.
e: This accurately describes the conditions under which coal is formed.

q: Coal is a uniform substance and its composition does not vary from deposit to deposit.
e: Coal is not a uniform substance; its composition varies from deposit to deposit.

q: Natural gas (methane) takes millions of years longer to form than coal.
e: The text states that natural gas does not take nearly as long to form as coal.

q: Methane is a common gas found in swamps and is also the by-product of animals' digestive system.
e: These are the specific natural sources of methane mentioned in the textbook.

q: Nuclear energy is non-renewable as the uranium fuels used are consumed in the nuclear fission reaction and hence are non-replenishable.
e: This explains exactly why nuclear energy is classified as non-renewable.

q: Nuclear energy is renewable because uranium fuels are easily replenished in a nuclear reactor.
e: Nuclear energy is non-renewable because uranium fuels are non-replenishable.

q: Energy produced in a nuclear reactor can be harnessed to produce electricity.
e: This is one of the primary uses of nuclear energy listed in the text.

q: Nuclear energy is also being used to power submarines and ship.
e: The text mentions vessels driven by nuclear energy can sail for long periods without refueling.

q: Radioisotopes obtained as by-products in nuclear reactions are used in medicine, agriculture and research.
e: These are the exact fields where radioisotope by-products are utilized.

q: Fossil fuel liquids are refined into petrochemical products used in the manufacture of plastics and polyurethane.
e: The text states petrochemicals are used to manufacture hundreds of products including plastics and polyurethane.

q: Fossil fuels are excellent sources of energy for our transportation needs.
e: The textbook explicitly states fossil fuels are excellent for transportation needs.

q: The fossil fuel industry extracts crude oil from the ground and converts it to gasoline.
e: This is given as an example of how fossil fuels are processed for transportation.
